beats.narration_text: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. Most people ask how to update a resume. The better question is where the resume lives.

show.event: types 'How do I update my resume?'
backspaces 'update' → 'where does it live' on the spoken correction

props.text:
How do I update
my resume?

beats.motion_claim: The writer types the maintenance question and corrects it into the one about where the truth is kept.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: Three terms. A resume dot JSON: your resume as named fields instead of prose, so each line can be checked. Attested: you read a field yourself and dated it. And generated output: a letter built from the record, meant to be thrown away.

terms.meaning: your resume as named fields, not prose — so every line can be pointed at and checked
you read the field yourself and dated it; nothing is true because a model wrote it
a cover letter or targeted resume built from the record, and meant to be discarded

qc.sparse_reason: TERMS card: three prerequisites, one line each.

beats.narration_text: Here is a resume as most people keep it. One document. You open it, edit it, save it. Every version writes over the one before.

shot.visual_intent: An isometric page sits on the cream stage with a few ink text lines; a pencil sweeps across it and the lines under the sweep are replaced. A faint ghost of the old lines fades out beneath. Label: resume.doc

show.event: the old lines fade to ghost and vanish

beats.motion_claim: The overwrite is the motion: the previous version disappears as the new one lands.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style (Bear, 2026-09-26): one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, with the voice carrying the explanation. The negative space is the style, so only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Now you ask a model to tune it for a job. It rewrites your bullets, tightens your verbs. And sometimes it adds a line you never wrote.

shot.visual_intent: The same page. Three ink lines lift, re-set slightly tighter, and settle. Then a FOURTH line slides in from off-stage and settles between two real ones, drawn in the same ink as the rest. No highlight, no marker.

show.event: a fourth line slides in and settles among them

beats.motion_claim: The inserted line arrives in the same ink and the same rhythm as the real ones — that is the whole danger.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style (Bear, 2026-09-26): one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, with the voice carrying the explanation. The negative space is the style, so only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: I have known students whose resumes claimed defense skills they did not have, because a model added them and nobody caught it. The page looked better, so it went out.

shot.visual_intent: Pull back: the page rides into an outbox tray. A magnifier passes over it and stops on the inserted line, which is indistinguishable from its neighbours; the magnifier moves on without stopping. Label: sent

show.event: magnifier passes over the inserted line

beats.motion_claim: The magnifier crossing the fake line without catching it is the claim: nothing on the page marks it as added.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style (Bear, 2026-09-26): one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, with the voice carrying the explanation. The negative space is the style, so only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: So keep it as data instead. One record, named fields: education, experience, skills, service. Every line is something you can point at and check.

shot.visual_intent: The page transforms into an isometric card of stacked field rows, each row a labelled slot: education, experience, skills, service. Rows drop in one at a time with a thin ink outline. Label: resume.json

show.event: the page becomes a stack of field rows

beats.motion_claim: Rows landing as named slots is the difference from prose: the structure is what makes a line checkable.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style (Bear, 2026-09-26): one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, with the voice carrying the explanation. The negative space is the style, so only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Then you read it yourself, line by line, and mark it attested, with a date. You are the only one who can say it is true.

shot.visual_intent: A cursor moves down the field rows; a terracotta check lands beside each as it passes. At the bottom a small slip stamps onto the card. Label beside the slip: attested · 2026-09-27

show.event: the attested slip stamps on with its date

beats.motion_claim: The checks land one per row, in order — verification is per line, not per document.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style (Bear, 2026-09-26): one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, with the voice carrying the explanation. The negative space is the style, so only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Now the letters come out of the record, not your last edit. A cover letter for this posting, a short resume for that one. The record stays. The output is disposable.

shot.visual_intent: The card stays centre-stage. Two thin pages peel off it and slide away to the right, each stamped with a small terracotta dot. The card is unchanged. Labels beside the pages: cover letter, targeted CV

show.event: first page peels off and slides away

beats.motion_claim: Pages leaving while the card stays put is the direction of the arrow: the record generates, never the reverse.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style (Bear, 2026-09-26): one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, with the voice carrying the explanation. The negative space is the style, so only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Mine was missing my committee work entirely. So I pulled it from the promotion dossier I had already written. Three committees, and a task team that surveyed six hundred and seventy-nine students.

shot.visual_intent: A binder stands beside the card with a visible gap in the card's field stack. Three pages lift out of the binder and drop into the gap, which closes. A small counter beside them climbs to 679.

show.event: binder appears; a gap shows in the stack
three pages lift out and drop into the gap

beats.motion_claim: The gap closing is the motion: the material already existed in another document and was simply absent from this one.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style (Bear, 2026-09-26): one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, with the voice carrying the explanation. The negative space is the style, so only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: And a section I had never written down: teaching other people's faculty to use a company's tools well. Twenty-five course assistants for courses I do not teach. Seven hundred learners in one course the Dean commissioned.

shot.visual_intent: A new field row grows onto the card, taller than the rest. Out of it, small server-lights fan out to a row of distant boxes that are NOT the card — other people's courses. A counter beside them climbs to 700.

show.event: the new row grows on the card
lights fan out to other courses

beats.motion_claim: The lights reaching boxes outside the card carries the claim: the work served courses that were not his.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style (Bear, 2026-09-26): one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, with the voice carrying the explanation. The negative space is the style, so only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Then the part I did not expect. My own job matcher reads four fields, and service is not one of them. The collector that searched three thousand postings never read the resume at all. A field no tool reads is one you have to say out loud yourself.

shot.visual_intent: The card again. A scan beam sweeps it, but only four rows light; the service and bridge-work rows stay grey as the beam passes over them. Beside the card, a separate stack of tiny postings has NO cable running to the card.

show.event: four rows light; two stay grey
the postings stack sits with no cable to the card

beats.motion_claim: The beam skipping two rows, and the missing cable, are both the finding: the data exists and nothing consumes it.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style (Bear, 2026-09-26): one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, with the voice carrying the explanation. The negative space is the style, so only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: Here is my resume as a document. Convert it to JSON with named fields for education, experience, skills, and service. Do not improve it, do not add anything, and do not reword my bullets. For every line you cannot source from what I gave you, put it in a list called unsourced instead of in the record. Then check two things. If the unsourced list is empty, did it drop something instead of flagging it? And is there a skill in the file you could not defend in an interview tomorrow? Cut it now, not then.
